our_argument_summary: WIN-008 claims a sharp 11.7 Hz telluric cutoff. Our review refutes this on three grounds: (1) the first Schumann harmonic at 14.3 Hz directly disproves any frequency ceiling at 11.7 Hz; (2) the 10–12 Hz dip is a standard inter-harmonic minimum of spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity physics (Chave & Jones 2012); (3) the dome’s f = c/(2D) formula reproduces 11.787 Hz only when D = 12,717 km, which matches Earth’s polar diameter to 0.03% and is not derivable from any documented dome parameter (firmament_height 9,086 km → 16.50 Hz; disc_radius 20,015 km → 7.49 Hz). Code analysis: monitor.py hardcodes the predicted/observed pair; no MT data is fetched. The detail block is shared with WIN-009 via detail_group="WIN-008/009".

holes_found.description: MATH ERROR — the "0.09% error" figure in detail_evidence is wrong by a factor of ~10. Our text reads: "hardcodes predicted = 11.788 Hz, observed = 11.7869 Hz (0.09% error, rounds to 0.0%)". Actual computation: |11.788 − 11.7869| = 0.0011 Hz; 0.0011 / 11.7869 = 9.33 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.0093%, which rounds to 0.01% (not 0.09%). The CONCLUSION ("rounds to 0.0%", trivially within the 1.0% tolerance) is unchanged regardless, so this does not damage the argument structure — but a numerically-literate dome defender could legitimately point at the specific quoted figure and say "your review can’t do percentage arithmetic." The c4 review carried the same 10× error ("0.011 Hz (0.093%)") into its findings — this is not a regression, it is a long-standing slip that the c4 round did not catch. Note: there is also a possible alternative reading where "0.09%" was intended as "0.0093%" with a typo dropping the leading zeros — but as written in the rendered HTML, readers see 0.09%, which is wrong.
holes_found.recommendation: Patch detail_evidence: replace "(0.09% error, rounds to 0.0%)" with either "(0.0093% error, trivially inside the 1.0% tolerance)" or, if you want to keep a single-digit form, "(<0.01% error, trivially inside the 1.0% tolerance)". The second form is shorter and conveys the same insight without forcing a reader to verify the exact value.

kernel_of_truth.description: The 10–12 Hz band is genuinely lower-power than the adjacent 7.83 Hz fundamental and 14.3 Hz first-harmonic Schumann peaks (data/wins.json:WIN-008.detail_evidence cites this directly). The dome correctly identifies a real feature of the ELF spectrum — there IS a measurable dip there. Independent of the dome model, peer-reviewed magnetotelluric literature documents the inter-harmonic minimum as a routine feature of the spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity (data/wins.json:WIN-008.detail_evidence cites Chave & Jones 2012, doi:10.1017/CBO9781139020138).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Three independent failure modes, each sufficient: (1) standard spherical-cavity physics fully predicts this inter-harmonic minimum without any dome geometry (data/wins.json:WIN-008.detail_evidence); (2) the dome’s formula f = c/(2D) reproduces 11.787 Hz only when D ≈ 12,717 km — Earth’s polar diameter, NOT any documented dome parameter (verified by direct computation; see quantitative_verification.computations); (3) the label "sharp cutoff" is directly falsified by the robust first Schumann harmonic at 14.3 Hz, routinely measured at monitoring stations worldwide (data/wins.json:WIN-008.detail_evidence). The kernel of truth is the dip; the dome’s "derivation" of it is a relabel of spherical-Earth geometry.

deeper_analysis: The c4→c5 drift is overwhelmingly positive — three of four c4 holes are now addressed. The polar-diameter precision (0.03% residual on 12,713.6 km) is materially stronger than c4’s mean-diameter-only framing (0.2% residual on 12,742 km), because a tighter residual is more probative: 0.03% is in the same range as professional satellite-geodesy uncertainty on Earth’s polar radius, which makes the parasitism claim much harder to dismiss as coincidence. The one new defect is the "0.09%" figure (hole [0]), which is a pure arithmetic slip and easy to fix. The c4 hole #4 boilerplate carryover and the WIN-009 parasitism propagation (c4 stronger_argument #1) both remain open but are low-priority polish items. Net assessment: the rewrite materially improves the argument; the verdict (Refuted by Data) holds with higher confidence than at c4.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A dome defender, fully conceding our methodological principles (internal consistency, discriminatory power, no default favoritism), can attempt three lines: (1) "12,717 km is not silently borrowed Earth diameter — it is the disc thickness, and the numerical near-coincidence with Earth’s polar diameter is a consequence of the dome’s flat-Earth model being calibrated to match astronomical observations at the equator, which forces certain length scales to converge on globe values. This is not parasitism; it is unavoidable calibration." Counter: this concedes the load-bearing point — the dome derivation does not stand on its own geometry, it stands on a calibrated match to globe-physics output. (2) "The first Schumann harmonic at 14.3 Hz is an ionospheric mode and does not falsify the disc-cavity 11.7 Hz cutoff because the disc and ionosphere are independent resonators." Counter: the dome has never published a two-cavity model; this is an ad-hoc patch invented to deflect this specific criticism. (3) "The math error in ‘0.09% error’ (hole [0]) shows the reviewers cannot do percentage arithmetic — their broader claims are suspect." Counter: this is a rhetorical attack on a single typo and does not touch the structural argument; we should preempt it by fixing the figure. Overall rating: 2 (defenses 1 and 2 require new dome content that doesn’t exist; defense 3 is a rhetorical jab that vanishes once the typo is fixed).
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Fix the "0.09% error" math (hole [0]) to remove defense 3 entirely. Do NOT add preemptive text against defenses 1 or 2 — both would require us to argue against unpublished dome content, which strawmans.
